title: Tenant Surge Credit Exchange — PRD for elastic burst credits and fairness controls
creator: Alex Moreno
description: Introduce a tenant-level Surge Credit Exchange: an operational mechanism that lets tenants accumulate, trade, and consume short-lived 'burst credits' to access additional dedicated capacity headroom during transient traffic spikes, while preserving isolation guarantees and predictable billing. This feature combines credit accrual, controlled transfer/escrow, automatic decay, and preemption safeguards to increase burst utility without degrading other tenants' SLOs.
goals: Enable tenants to safely burst above reserved capacity for short intervals using credit balances
Reduce hard preemptions and failed requests during transient load by offering graceful credit-based capacity access
Expose transparent telemetry and accounting in the Console and billing reports
Provide guardrails so burst consumption cannot cause downstream SLA violations for co-tenants or Platform-managed system services
non_goals: Replace existing reserved-pool contracts or committed capacity pricing
Support unbounded cross-tenant credit pooling (no shared pools across customers)
Implement a full marketplace with external trading between unrelated customers in the initial launch
background: Engineering has observed recurring transient hotspots where tenants exhaust reserved pool tokens and are subject to immediate request preemption or large latency regressions. Existing 'soft reserve' mechanisms either over-provision or cause noisy preemption. A credit-based exchange allows predictable, auditable temporary headroom while enabling conservative preemption policies tied to credit state.
detailed_requirements: Credit model: 1 credit = 1 second * vCPU-equivalent unit of capacity (abstract unit mapped to model throughput; conversion table per flavor is documented).

Accrual: Tenants accrue credits over time as a function of unused reservation headroom (daily accrual cap configurable per account). Accrual rate defaults to 2% of reserved capacity per day up to a tenant cap (configurable).
Purchase/Top-up: Tenants can purchase burst credits via API/Console with immediate availability. Purchased credits are billed separately and flagged in accounting records.
Escrow & Transfer: Tenants can move credits into a short-lived escrow for an internal sub-tenant (org/team) with strict audit logs. Transfers between independent customer accounts are disabled in v1.
Decay/Expiry: Credits decay with a half-life policy and expire after 90 days by default. Decay schedule and expiry window are configurable at account level via enterprise contract.

Consumption: When a request exceeds reserved allocation, system consumes credits preferentially from purchased credits then accrued credits. Consumption is metered per-request and visible in streaming traces.

Preemption Policy: If credits deplete, degrade latency-aware fallbacks (model variant switch, reduced max_tokens) are applied before hard-killing requests. Only if fallbacks fail do we preempt; preemptions must include reason codes and affected tokens count.

Fairness throttle: Global fairness controller ensures tenants consuming burst credits cannot starve co-tenants; a sliding-window fairness score reduces burst throughput if cross-tenant latency/erro rates exceed thresholds.
Console UX: New 'Burst credits' panel with balance, accrual forecast, purchase flow, recent consumption timeline, and alerts for low-balance and approaching expiry.

APIs: add endpoints: GET /v1/accounts/{id}/burst-credits, POST /v1/accounts/{id}/burst-credits/purchase, POST /v1/accounts/{id}/burst-credits/transfer, GET /v1/accounts/{id}/burst-credits/consumption (streaming).

Telemetry: Emit standardized metrics: burst_credits_balance, burst_credits_accrued, burst_credits_consumed, burst_credit_preemptions, burst_credit_decay_events. Correlate to tenant_id, model_flavor, zone.
Billing: Purchased credits show as a line item in invoices; consumed accrued credits are reconciled monthly and can be credited back if post-facto autoscaling reduced consumption (adjustment window).

Security & Audit: All transfers, purchases, and consumption events must be logged to audit trail with actor, ip, timestamp, and reason. Sensitive operations require RBAC check  and optional SSO scope extension.
acceptance_criteria: A: Credit balance appears in Console for test tenant and matches API GET balance within 5 seconds of any operation
B: Purchase flow: POST purchase returns 200, balance increases immediately, and an invoice line item is generated in test billing environment
C: Consumption: under synthetic spike that exceeds reserved capacity, system consumes credits and applies a fallback strategy before any request is preempted
D: Preemption audit: when a preemption occurs, a preemption event with reason code 'CREDIT_EXHAUST' is recorded and surfaced in per-route telemetry

E: Fairness: in a two-tenant synthetic scenario, tenant A consuming >80% of spare capacity for 10 minutes triggers fairness throttle and measurable reduction in A's burst throughput without increased error rate for tenant B
F: Decay: create credits, wait 30 days in test harness (timewarp), confirm decay applied per configured half-life schedule
G: API contract: all new endpoints exist, pass schema validation, and have OpenAPI docs linked from Console
H: Security: RBAC prevents non-admin user from performing account-level transfers in test scenarios and audit logs contain required fields
metrics: 95th percentile burst latency during spikes (goal: no more than 1.2x baseline when credits used)
Monthly burn rate of purchased vs accrued credits
Number of preemptions with reason=CREDIT_EXHAUST (goal: reduce by 60% for target tenants)
ux_requirements: Console must show color-coded balance (green >30d equivalent, amber 7-30d, red <7d), tooltip explaining accrual/purchase/expiry
Purchase modal with immediate cost estimate, purchase confirmation and link to invoice preview
Admin audit view listing transfers and escrow actions with CSV export
In-route toast for SDK users: 'Burst credit used — X remaining' (configurable opt-out)
Clear documentation in Quickstart about how credits interact with autoscaling and preemption
api_contracts: GET /v1/accounts/{id}/burst-credits/consumption -> streaming events: {timestamp, request_id, credits_used, reason}
Note: exact response schemas documented in OpenAPI spec; fields above are summary strings for this PRD.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta, 2 weeks): internal tenants + opt-in customers. Expose API & Console read-only, allow purchases for billing teams only.
Phase 2 (limited GA, 6 weeks): enable transfers to sub-accounts, expose purchase flow to all paid tenants, enable fairness controller with conservative thresholds.
Phase 3 (GA): enable full decay config, billing reconciliation, and guardrail tuning based on telemetry.
risks: Overcomplicated UX causing customer confusion — mitigate with clear defaults and inline docs
Adversarial load patterns could try to game accrual; require fraud detection heuristics and rate limits
Incorrect conversion table between credits and capacity could lead to unexpected billing — mitigation: conservative mapping and e2e tests
Cross-tenant fairness controller tuning may cause false positives and reduce legitimate burst — require A/B rollouts and knobs
implementation_notes: Work in runtime: add credit-aware admission hook that consults per-tenant credit state before granting additional tokens
Telemetry: wire credit metrics into Console cost panel and per-route traces
Billing: create provisional invoice line item semantics for purchased credits and ensure test-mode purchases do not bill production accounts
Feature flag gating for early rollouts and killswitch for immediate disablement
qa_plan: Unit tests for accrual/purchase/consumption accounting logic
Integration test: synthetic spike harness with timewarp to validate decay/expiry
Load test: multi-tenant fairness scenario and automated comparison against baseline preemptions
Security test: RBAC checks and audit trail verification
